switches.summary: Disable verbose Claude Code permission prompts.
switches.description: When off, Claude Code does not enumerate every tool call as a discrete permission prompt. Reduces noise while keeping core safety gates in place.

switches.summary: Prefer Supabase and Vercel CLIs over MCP or REST.
switches.description: Arkira-governed projects prefer first-party CLIs for connector work because they ship with auth, tracing, and stable contracts. When on, hooks and skills steer Claude toward the CLI path.

switches.summary: Require server-side authentication and authorization validation.
switches.description: When on, hooks and skills treat server-side auth validation, tenant membership checks, role checks, and resource ownership checks as required review targets for protected behavior, and treat Supabase Auth as the default provider for Supabase-backed apps with one auth system per app. Reference implementation: examples/auth-reference/.

switches.summary: Require secret exposure checks before accepting security-sensitive work.
switches.description: When on, hooks and skills require explicit checks for committed secrets, browser-exposed server secrets, logged credentials, service-role exposure, and production secrets in unsafe contexts.

switches.summary: Require local, preview, and production environment separation checks.
switches.description: When on, hooks and skills require review of environment scoping, preview and production secret separation, and production deployment variable readiness before production-oriented changes are accepted.

switches.summary: Keep Lens Mode disabled by default in production.
switches.description: When on, hooks and skills flag production Lens Mode, role switching, or support impersonation as approval-sensitive unless the workflow is explicit, documented, logged, and constrained.

switches.summary: Require explicit confirmation for destructive admin and Lens Mode actions.
switches.description: When on, hooks and skills require destructive actions during admin access or Lens Mode to preserve actor identity, log the action, and require explicit confirmation.

switches.summary: Require audit logging for admin, support, and Lens Mode activity.
switches.description: When on, hooks and skills expect admin and Lens Mode workflows to preserve actor identity, effective identity, target organization, action, timestamp, and support context where practical.

switches.summary: Report CLI freshness and apply tracked upgrades on demand.
switches.description: The explicit report path checks tracked CLIs (vercel, supabase, gh, node, pnpm, git, bun, wrangler) against their latest published versions. It reports safe gaps, major gaps, and absent tools for manual action. The report mode (`--report`) is read only and never invokes an installer. `--apply` is the explicit path that runs tracked installers for installed tools.

switches.summary: Strongly advise parallel subagents when work fans out.
switches.description: When on, hosts may dispatch at most three independent read-only units when parallel work reduces elapsed time or top-level context. Every unit uses an explicit economical model. Writers remain serial, and unavailable subagent dispatch degrades to a reported sequential run. The switch is policy guidance because no repository hook can force host fanout. See governance/agent-swarm-standard.md.

switches.summary: End task responses with a recommended-next-move trailer.
switches.description: When on, every response that finishes or pauses a task ends with a three-line block: Recommended (one sentence), Alternate (one or two sentences, optional), Gate (any approval needed, or 'none'). Mid-turn clarifications, pure acknowledgements, and one-line answers are exempt. When off, the trailer is omitted. See governance/next-steps-standard.md.

switches.summary: Reflect on each session and propose CLAUDE.md updates (propose-only).
switches.description: When on, a Stop hook reflects on a session that changed tracked files and writes proposed CLAUDE.md edits to .arkira/proposals/claude-md/ for human review. It never edits CLAUDE.md and runs reflection in the background so it never delays the session. A SessionStart hook surfaces pending proposals. Off by default because reflection spends model tokens. See governance/self-improving-standard.md.

switches.summary: Select explicit models and effort for whole-task quality, time, and tokens.
switches.description: When on, every role-runtime dispatch resolves an explicit provider, model, and effort using the canonical model catalog. Choose for the complete path through implementation, review, validation, retries, and rework. Quality, security, and verified completion are acceptance gates; monetary cost is secondary unless the operator sets a budget. Honor explicit operator settings, verify native availability, and never silently substitute. See governance/model-selection-standard.md for defaults and escalation.

switches.summary: Enforce token-only styling; flag raw hex and hardcoded themed values.
switches.description: When on, reviews and skills flag raw hex colors and hardcoded Tailwind literals for themed values, and expect components to consume semantic tokens per theme/theme-standard.md. Brand and dark-mode changes must be token changes, not component changes. See theme/theme-standard.md.

switches.summary: Require full phone and tablet support for every app.
switches.description: When on, reviews and skills treat mobile compliance as a release gate per mobile/mobile-compliance-standard.md: 320px reflow with no horizontal scroll, a 44px touch-target floor, safe-area handling, zoom never disabled, tablet as a first-class layout, and a mobile performance budget. Ties into the accessibility-review skill. See mobile/mobile-compliance-standard.md.

switches.summary: Prefer language-server symbol navigation over grep when available.
switches.description: When on, Claude uses the TypeScript language server (go-to-definition, find-references, rename, symbol search) for symbol-shaped lookups instead of grep, and reserves grep for text and non-symbol search. Requires the code-intelligence plugin and a language-server binary per tooling/lsp-standard.md. The binary is a per-machine install, so this is guidance the agent follows when a server is available.

switches.summary: Reserved switch for non-operational autonomous self-heal.
switches.description: Autonomous self-heal is not operational in this release. This switch has no apply, merge, revert, branch, stage, or commit effect. Proposals remain human-reviewed. See governance/self-improving-standard.md.

switches.summary: Write an automatic session checkpoint at a configurable interval.
switches.description: When on, a Stop hook writes a checkpoint of git facts to auto-memory once the configured interval has elapsed since the last checkpoint, so a long session with no merges can still be resumed after a session clear. The interval defaults to 120 minutes and is set via .arkira/config.json checkpoint.interval_minutes or the ARKIRA_TIME_CHECKPOINT_MINUTES environment variable. Off by default. The /checkpoint command writes one on demand regardless of this switch. See governance/checkpoint-standard.md.

switches.summary: Require sanctioned native app approach, shared tokens, and store/release gates.
switches.description: When on, reviews and skills treat the native app standard as a release gate per mobile/native-app-standard.md: Expo + React Native (New Architecture) as the default approach with Capacitor allowed only as a 4.2-mitigated fast-path, design tokens shared with web via Style Dictionary, accessibility and touch-target parity, store readiness (privacy labels, permission strings, metadata), a portal/reader payments model (no in-app sale of web memberships, IAP only where required, region-aware steering), and EAS build/submit/OTA discipline (OTA carries JS/asset changes only). Ties into design-system and the accessibility checklist of production-audit. See mobile/native-app-standard.md.

switches.summary: Hold every change to the four core engineering principles.
switches.description: When on, Claude and Codex hold every change to four principles per governance/root-agents.md: Think Before Coding (understand the system and form a plan before editing), Simplicity First (prefer the simplest design that works; no speculative abstraction), Surgical Changes (touch only what the task requires; no opportunistic refactor), and Goal-Driven (every change traces to the stated objective and is verified against it). The principles bind both audit and implementation mode and reinforce the existing minimal-change and verify-don't-assume rules. See governance/root-agents.md.

switches.summary: Nudge a non-default execution mode on high-confidence prompts.
switches.description: When on, a UserPromptSubmit hook (hooks/mode-suggest.sh) classifies the submitted prompt with high-precision, heuristic-only patterns and, on an unambiguous match, adds one advisory line nudging a non-default execution mode: a Workflow / ultracode for broad fan-out (whole-repo audits, sweeps, migrations) or /goal for a single end-to-end objective (plan -> review -> build -> verify). It never nudges the default (plain/inline), never calls a model, and stays silent on the vast majority of prompts; a loose keyword like 'workflow' alone does not fire. Off by default because prompt-time nudges become ignored wallpaper unless quiet. Governs execution mode, paired with but distinct from the model-tier policy in governance/model-selection-standard.md. See governance/mode-routing-standard.md.

switches.summary: Legacy eval preference retained for configuration compatibility.
switches.description: Compatibility-only in this release. The runner does not read this switch. Ordinary non-release evals report their actual result, while the release review path always requires a verified semantic judge and exact-candidate artifact regardless of this value. Evals apply to non-deterministic agent output and trajectories, never to deterministic application code covered by a unit test. See governance/eval-standard.md.

switches.summary: Check vendored third-party components for upstream updates.
switches.description: When explicitly enabled in repo-local config, a SessionStart hook and /arkira-sync report when vendored skills, agents, tools, or plugins fall behind their pinned upstream. Unconfigured and unrelated projects stay silent and state-free. Detection only; updates are prepared as reviewed diffs and never auto-merged.

switches.summary: Require waterfall-free, isolated React server data flows.
switches.description: When on, app repos follow react/data-fetching-standard.md for async parallelism, RSC fetching and caching, request isolation, and minimal server-to-client serialization.

switches.summary: Require disciplined React bundles, renders, and hydration.
switches.description: When on, app repos follow react/bundle-rendering-standard.md for narrow bundles, stable component identity, efficient updates, and non-blocking client rendering and hydration.

switches.summary: Require composable React 19 component architecture.
switches.description: When on, app repos follow react/composition-standard.md for compound components, provider-owned injectable state, explicit variants, and React 19 ref and context idioms.

switches.summary: Require purposeful, token-driven React view transitions.
switches.description: When on, app repos follow react/motion-standard.md for native ViewTransition patterns, meaningful animation choices, navigation-path verification, and semantic motion-token styling.

switches.summary: Expose the experimental high-assurance release workflow.
switches.description: When on, operators may opt into the experimental high-assurance appendix after satisfying Elevated review. It is not authoritative release proof while the trust defects tracked in docs/specs/2026-07-22-release-trust-producers.md remain open.
